land.text: Chios, which Benedetto I Zaccaria 'reconquered... in 1304'

predecessors.note: Andronikos II 'acknowledged the occupation, first for 10 years, then renewed at five-year intervals' (Martino Zaccaria page): a renewable concession, not a cession.

land.text: Chios, from which the locals expelled the Zaccaria in 1329 (Chios page) when Andronikos III arrived with 105 vessels; Samos and Kos: page silent

successors.note: Andronikos III made Kalothetos governor of Chios. Genoa returned in 1346 as the Maona (maona-of-chios).

capitals.name: Chios (Kastro)
capitals.note: Page silent on a capital; the citadel of Chios town is where Martino 'locked himself in his citadel' in 1329.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row). Chios alone: 'Benedetto I Zaccaria, a Genoese admiral, reconquered the island in 1304 and kept it as a renewable concession, founding the short-lived Lordship of Chios.' No area on the page.

correction.text: Chios, Samos and Kos: of the lands Philip II granted Martino in 1325 'only the first three were already under Zaccaria control'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Chios, Samos and Kos. In 1325 Philip II (titular Latin emperor) named Martino 'King and Despot of Asia Minor' and gave him Chios, Samos, Kos, Lesbos, Ikaria, Tenedos, Oinousses and Marmara; the page says 'only the first three were already under Zaccaria control; the rest were held by the Byzantines or Turks'. The other Zaccaria holdings on the mainland (the barony of Chalandritsa in the Morea, Veligosti-Damala) are not Chios and are not drawn here.

ledger.note: 1304: Benedetto I Zaccaria seizes Chios. 'Benedetto I Zaccaria, a Genoese admiral, reconquered the island in 1304' and held it as a renewable concession; the Martino Zaccaria page: 'Benedetto I captured Chios from the Byzantines. Andronikos II acknowledged the occupation, first for 10 years, then renewed at five-year intervals'.

region.text: Samos and Kos, 'already under Zaccaria control' when Philip II named Martino 'King and Despot of Asia Minor' in 1325

ledger.note: 1325: Martino's reach grows to Samos and Kos. Bridging: the page says only that Samos and Kos were already Zaccaria in 1325, with no year or previous holder; Byzantine overlordship is the researcher's reading. The 1325 grants of Lesbos, Ikaria, Tenedos, Oinousses and Marmara were titles on paper.

1329: Chios is lost. 'Locals responded to a letter from the emperor and expelled the Zaccaria family in 1329'; the Martino page: in autumn Andronikos III sailed to Chios with 105 vessels, Martino sank his three galleys, locked himself in his citadel and surrendered; the emperor spared his life and took him to Constantinople.

1329: Samos and Kos follow Chios. Bridging: the page says only that the 1329 expedition ended Martino's lordship of Chios and that Phocaea acknowledged Andronikos's suzerainty; it is silent on Samos and Kos.

region.text: Chios, Samos and Kos: of the lands Philip II granted Martino in 1325 'only the first three were already under Zaccaria control'

ledger.note: 1329: the Zaccaria lordship of Chios ends. 'The 1329 end of his lordship is the page's last account of Chios under his rule'; Martino was released in 1337 and killed at Smyrna on 17 January 1345.

wars.name: Byzantine reconquest of Chios
wars.outcome: Andronikos III sailed to Chios in autumn 1329 with 105 vessels; Martino Zaccaria refused a garrison and tribute, was besieged in his citadel and surrendered; the emperor made Kalothetos governor.
wars.note: The Chios page says the locals expelled the Zaccaria after a letter from the emperor; the Martino page has the fleet.

certainty.note: An island lordship: the coast is the border; Samos and Kos are listed on one page with no dates.

notes: Written by eu-05-x (additions). Cliopatria has no row; slug free. No Wikipedia article named 'Lordship of Chios' was opened (the Chios page uses the phrase), so wikipedia is null; a gap-filler may link the Zaccaria family article. Two pages opened. Not settled: the lordship's end month (autumn 1329), Samos's and Kos's fate, and Phocaea (Foça page: a Genoese fief from the Byzantine emperor in 1275, Zaccaria alum concessions in 1267; Andronikos III forced Phocaea to acknowledge his suzerainty in 1329), which belongs to a Lordship of Phocaea no dossier covers yet. Kos is also a Hospitaller island (hospitaller-rhodes dossier); the Hospitaller page is silent on when they got it. Samos and Kos coordinates are used (not in the gazetteer).
